segments.text: Posed by Pierre de Fermat to Evangelista Torricelli, X thirteen is the First Isogonic Center, or Fermat Point: erect outward equilateral triangles on sides B C, C A, and A B, join their outer apexes to the opposite vertices A, B, and C, and those three segments of equal length concur at X thirteen.

segments.text: At X thirteen, each side of triangle A B C subtends an equal angle of one hundred twenty degrees, minimizing the sum of distances P A plus P B plus P C whenever every angle of A B C is less than one hundred twenty degrees. Its trilinear coordinates are cosecant of A plus pi over three, to cosecant of B plus pi over three, to cosecant of C plus pi over three.
